Unsa ang labing layo nga gibuhat sa tawo gikan sa Earth?

Voyager 1! Gilusad niadtong 1977, nagbiyahe kini lapas sa tanang planeta paingon sa wanang taliwala sa mga bituon.

Malaki at makulay na orkidyang tumutubo lang sa mga gubat ng Mindanao, kaya't tinatawag itong 'Reyna ng mga Orkidya' ng Pilipinas.

Because their body heat stays steady no matter the weather, warm-blooded animals can keep moving and hunting even on cold nights.

Dahil panatag ang init ng kanilang katawan, kayang manatiling aktibo ang mga hayop na mainit ang dugo kahit malamig na gabi.

No! Wasps and hornets don't make honey — the sweet honey we eat comes only from honeybees.

Hindi! Hindi gumagawa ng pulot ang putakti at hornet — ang masarap na pulot ay galing lang sa pukyutan.

Dili! Ang putakti ug hornet dili maghimo og dugos — ang tam-is nga dugos gikan ra sa putyukan.

What's really inside a wasp's sting?

It's not just one substance! Wasp venom is a mix of chemicals and proteins that cause pain and swelling — that's why the sting burns right away.

Hindi lang isang sangkap ang kamandag ng putakti. Halo ito ng iba't ibang kemikal at protina na nagpapasakit at nagpapamaga — kaya parang nag-aapoy pagkatapos masaksak.

Unsa gyud ang sulod sa hilo sa putyukan?

Dili lang usa ka butang ang hilo sa putyukan. Sagol kini sa lain-laing kemikal ug protina nga maghatag og kasakit ug paghubag — mao nga mura'g nagdilaab human matusok.

In Fahrenheit, water boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!

Sa Fahrenheit, kumukulo ang tubig sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!

Sa Fahrenheit, magbukal ang tubig sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!

copy.bis: Ang tubig mogahi (mahimong yelo) sa 32 °F (32 degrees Fahrenheit)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water boils hotter than 100 degrees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions boiling (a change of state) but does not describe changes of state using diagrams or flowcharts as required, and the focus is on pressure raising the boiling point, not on the processes of melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water boils hotter than 100 degrees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about pressure raising the boiling point, not about how changes in temperature cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It does not directly support the competency's skill of describing temperature-driven state changes.

copy.en: In a pressure cooker, trapped steam raises the pressure! Water boils hotter than 100 degrees, cooking tough foods like beef or mung beans much faster.
copy.tl: Sa pressure cooker, naiipit ang singaw kaya tumataas ang presyon! Kumukulo ang tubig nang mas mainit sa 100 degrees, kaya mas mabilis maluto ang beef o monggo.
copy.bis: Sa pressure cooker, ma-ipit ang alisngaw mao nga mosaka ang presyon! Mobukal ang tubig nga mas init pa sa 100 degrees, mao nga mas paspas maluto ang karne o monggo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside water, molecules are pulled on all sides, but at the surface, nothing pulls upward, making the clinging stronger to create surface tension.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains cohesion and surface tension, which involves particles attracting each other, but it does not describe particles being in motion, having spaces between them, or moving faster with temperature. It only touches on the attraction aspect without addressing the other required characteristics of the particle model.

copy.en: Cohesion and surface tension are linked! Inside water, molecules are pulled on all sides, but at the surface, nothing pulls upward, making the clinging stronger to create surface tension.
copy.tl: Magkaugnay ang cohesion at surface tension! Sa loob, hinihila ang mga molekula sa lahat ng panig, pero sa ibabaw, walang humihila pataas kaya mas mariin ang pagkakapit para mabuo ang surface tension.
copy.bis: Magkadugtong ang cohesion ug surface tension! Sa sulod, gibira ang mga molekula sa tanang kilid, apan sa ibabaw, walay mobira pataas mao nga mas kusog ang pagkupot aron mahimo ang surface tension.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water has low viscosity!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes viscosity and flow rate of water, which is a property of liquids but not the specific property of shape and volume required by G5-M-3. It does not address definite/indefinite shape or volume for solids, liquids, or gases.

copy.en:
Why is water so easy to pour?

Water has low viscosity! This means it flows very fast and is super easy to pour.
copy.tl:
Bakit madaling ibuhos ang tubig?

Ang tubig ay may mababang viscosity! Kaya mabilis itong dumaloy at napakadaling ibuhos.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga sayon ibubo ang tubig?

Ang tubig adunay ubos nga viscosity! Mao nga paspas kini modagayday ug sayon kaayo ibubo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: feel the water pressure on your ears
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water pressure increasing with depth, which is an example of a force acting on the body, but it does not address the competency's core idea that forces act between objects and can be measured. No measurement or general force concept is taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The deeper you go, the stronger it gets because more water above you presses down
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about water pressure and depth, not about the shape and volume properties of solids, liquids, and gases. It does not describe definite/indefinite shape or volume for any state of matter.

copy.en: Dive deep in a pool and feel the water pressure on your ears! The deeper you go, the stronger it gets because more water above you presses down.
copy.tl: Sumisid ka ba sa malalim na pool? Mararamdaman mo ang water pressure sa tainga! Mas lalim ka, mas malakas ang presyon dahil mas maraming tubig ang pumipilit sa iyo.
copy.bis: Pag lubog nimo sa lawom nga pool, mabati nimo ang water pressure sa tainga! Mas lawom ka, mas kusog ang presyon tungod kay mas daghang tubig ang nagduso sa imo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made mostly of water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions watermelon is mostly water, but does not teach the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or how matter exists in these states. It only touches on water as a liquid, which is not direct support for identifying the three states.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: green outside and red inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the fruit's outer and inner appearance, but does not address the outer parts of plants such as leaves, roots, and stems, nor their roles in getting water and nutrients. The fruit is not one of the specified plant parts.

copy.en: Watermelon is a big fruit, green outside and red inside, made mostly of water — that's why it's so refreshing on a hot day.
copy.tl: Ang pakwan ay malaking prutas, berde sa labas at pula sa loob, na halos puro tubig — kaya nakaka-preskong kainin tuwing tag-init.
copy.bis: Ang pakwan usa ka dako nga prutas, lunhaw sa gawas ug pula sa sulod, nga halos puro tubig — mao nga makapabugnaw kaonon panahon sa init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This number shows exactly how much electricity it uses at each moment.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: collaborate in a class discussion to identify ways to reduce the use of electrical energy in Filipino houses and communities and explain what local and global benefits can be achieved
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains what watts measure (instantaneous electricity use), which is background knowledge for understanding energy consumption. It does not identify ways to reduce electrical energy use or explain local/global benefits, which are the actions in the competency.

copy.en: Look at the watts on an appliance! This number shows exactly how much electricity it uses at each moment.
copy.tl: Tingnan ang watts sa isang aparato! Ang bilang na ito ang nagpapakita kung gaano karaming kuryente ang ginagamit nito kada sandali.
copy.bis: Tan-awa ang watts sa usa ka aparato! Ang gidaghanon niini magpakita kung pila ka koryente ang gigamit niini sa matag higayon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The P-wave reaches sensors first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses seismic P-waves and S-waves arriving at sensors, but does not teach that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver. The energy-transfer concept is not addressed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earthquakes have a fast P-wave and a slower S-wave!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some examples of longitudinal waves, and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card names P-waves and S-waves but does not identify them as longitudinal or transverse waves, so it does not directly support identifying examples of longitudinal and transverse waves.

copy.en: Earthquakes have a fast P-wave and a slower S-wave! The P-wave reaches sensors first, giving the Philippines an early warning before the damaging S-wave arrives.
copy.tl: May mabilis na P-wave at mabagal na S-wave ang lindol! Umaabot muna ang P-wave sa sensors, nagbibigay ng maagang babala sa Pilipinas bago dumating ang mapaminsalang S-wave.
copy.bis: Adunay paspas nga P-wave ug hinay nga S-wave sa linog! Mu-abot una ang P-wave sa mga sensor, muhatag og sayong pasidaan sa Pilipinas una pa ang makadaot nga S-wave.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The air you breathe out carries water vapor — that's why breathing on a cold mirror leaves a thin film of fog!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water vapor and fog, which is an example of condensation, but it does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) nor use diagrams/flowcharts as required by the competency. It only touches on the phenomenon without teaching the state-change process.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The air you breathe out carries water vapor — that's why breathing on a cold mirror leaves a thin film of fog!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies a temperature-related change (cold mirror causing fog), but it does not explicitly describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state, nor does it cover the solid-liquid-gas progression. It is only a passing example of condensation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The air you breathe out carries water vapor
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water vapor (a gas) but does not identify the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases) or their existence. It does not directly support the competency of identifying that matter exists in three states.

copy.en:
Why does a mirror fog up when you breathe on it?

The air you breathe out carries water vapor — that's why breathing on a cold mirror leaves a thin film of fog!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagkaka-hamog ang salamin kapag hiningahan?

May kasamang singaw ng tubig ang hininga mong palabas — kaya kapag hiningahan mo ang malamig na salamin, namumuo ang manipis na hamog!
copy.bis:
Nganong magabon ang salamin kon huypan nimo?

Ang hangin nga imong gibuga adunay alisngaw sa tubig — mao nga kon huypan nimo ang bugnaw nga salamin, mamugna ang nipis nga gabon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: light bounces off them and travels straight into our eyes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a general fact about seeing non-luminous objects by reflected light. It does not involve mirrors, refraction, lenses, prisms, or guided investigations, which are the core actions of G8-F-11.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: light bounces off them and travels straight into our eyes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how light behaves (reflection) but does not explore sources of light, how it can be changed, or its uses in everyday situations. It is a single factual statement, not a guided activity or exploration.

copy.en: We see objects that do not glow because light bounces off them and travels straight into our eyes!
copy.tl: Nakikita natin ang mga bagay na hindi nagliliwanag dahil tumatalbog ang liwanag mula sa mga ito papunta sa ating mga mata!
copy.bis: Makita nato ang mga butang nga dili mosiga tungod kay ang kahayag motalbog gikan niini paingon sa atong mga mata!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The IPCC is an international group of scientists that regularly assesses the latest knowledge about climate change!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes what the IPCC is and that it assesses climate change knowledge. It does not present or identify any evidence of global warming or climate change, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Governments use their important reports to help with planning.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions government planning but does not identify local impacts of global climate change or suggest individual actions to reduce global warming. It is only tangentially related to the competency's topic.

copy.en:
What is the IPCC?

The IPCC is an international group of scientists that regularly assesses the latest knowledge about climate change! Governments use their important reports to help with planning.
copy.tl:
Ano ang IPCC?

Ang IPCC ay isang internasyonal na grupo ng mga siyentipiko na regular na nag-aassess ng pinakabagong kaalaman tungkol sa climate change! Ginagamit ng mga pamahalaan ang kanilang mga ulat para sa pagpaplano.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang IPCC?

Ang IPCC usa ka internasyonal nga grupo sa mga siyentipiko nga regular nga nag-assess sa pinakabag-o nga kaalaman bahin sa climate change! Gigamit sa mga gobyerno ang ilang mga ulat alang sa pagpaplano.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Big storms are watched from space using a weather satellite
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a map and a record of tracking data to trace the path of typhoons that enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that storms are watched from space by a weather satellite. It does not involve a map, tracking data, or tracing typhoon paths within the PAR, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Big storms are watched from space using a weather satellite
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions storm monitoring but does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. It shares the typhoon topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Big storms are watched from space using a weather satellite orbiting high above Earth!
copy.tl: Ang malalaking bagyo ay binabantayan mula sa kalawakan gamit ang weather satellite na umiikot sa itaas!
copy.bis: Ang dagkong bagyo gibantayan gikan sa kawanangan gamit ang weather satellite nga nagtuyok sa ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A weather station sits on the ground, measuring weather at one exact spot.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that a weather station measures weather, but it does not teach how to use weather instruments to measure and record characteristics of weather during a school day. It only gives a general description of what a weather station does, without any instrument names, measurement procedures, or recording activities.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A weather satellite floats in space, photographing clouds and storms from above.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions storms and weather satellites, but it does not describe weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by PAGASA. There is no reference to PAGASA, warning signals, or how to interpret them.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Together, they make better forecasts!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses weather forecasting and the roles of ground stations and satellites, but it does not involve examining a local weather chart, making interpretations about local weather, or describing/practicing safety precautions for poor or extreme weather. The content is only tangentially related to weather interpretation.

copy.en: A weather station sits on the ground, measuring weather at one exact spot. A weather satellite floats in space, photographing clouds and storms from above. Together, they make better forecasts!
copy.tl: Ang weather station ay nasa lupa, sumusukat ng panahon sa isang lugar. Ang weather satellite ay nasa kalawakan, nagkuha ng larawan ng ulap at bagyo. Magkatulong sila para sa mas magandang forecast!
copy.bis: Ang weather station naa sa yuta, magsukod sa panahon sa usa ka dapit. Ang weather satellite naa sa kawanangan, mokuha og hulagway sa panganod ug bagyo. Magtinabangay sila alang sa mas maayong forecast!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A tropical depression is the earliest and weakest stage of a tropical cyclone!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about the weakest stage of a tropical cyclone, but the competency requires gathering information from secondary sources to explain how typhoons develop and why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. The card does not explain the development process or the Philippines' proneness, and it does not involve secondary-source gathering. It is only tangentially related to typhoon development.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its wind speed is below 62 km/h, but it can grow into a typhoon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone. The card only states that a tropical depression is the weakest stage with wind speed below 62 km/h and can grow into a typhoon. It does not describe weather conditions before, during, or after a cyclone, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A tropical depression is the earliest and weakest stage of a tropical cyclone! Its wind speed is below 62 km/h, but it can grow into a typhoon.
copy.tl: Ang tropical depression ang pinakamaaga at pinakamahinang yugto ng isang tropical cyclone! Ang bilis ng hangin ay mas mababa sa 62 km/h, pero pwede itong lumago sa bagyo.
copy.bis: Ang tropical depression mao ang pinakaunang ug pinakamahinang yugto sa usa ka tropical cyclone! Ang bilis sa hangin ubos sa 62 km/h, pero mahimong motubo sa bagyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weather instruments measure the weather day by day.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions weather instruments and weather but does not identify any specific weather characteristics (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, rain, cloud cover) required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weather instruments measure the weather day by day.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to weather instruments measuring weather but does not describe using them to measure and record characteristics during a school day; it focuses on long-term climate, not the school-day measurement skill.

copy.en: Weather instruments measure the weather day by day. But when we combine their readings over many years, they reveal a place's climate!
copy.tl: Sinusukat ng weather instruments ang panahon araw-araw. Pero kapag pinagsama-sama ang readings sa maraming taon, naipapakita nito ang climate ng isang lugar!
copy.bis: Nagsukod ang weather instruments sa panahon adlaw-adlaw. Apan kon tigumon ang ilang readings sulod sa daghang tuig, mapakita niini ang climate sa usa ka dapit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of repeated heating and cooling, their thin outer layers slowly peel off! This awesome process is called exfoliation.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains exfoliation, a weathering process that breaks rocks into smaller pieces. Weathering is a precursor to soil formation, but the card does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals, nor does it mention soil, minerals, or the soil-forming process. It provides useful background but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
Why do some big rocks peel like an onion?

Because of repeated heating and cooling, their thin outer layers slowly peel off! This awesome process is called exfoliation.
copy.tl:
Bakit ba ang ilang malalaking bato ay natutuklap parang sibuyas?

Dahil sa paulit-ulit na pag-init at paglamig, ang manipis na panlabas na bahagi ay unti-unting natutuklap! Tinatawag itong exfoliation.
copy.bis:
Nganong ang ubang dagkong bato mangalukab man sama sa sibuyas?

Tungod sa balik-balik nga pag-init ug pagbugnaw, ang nipis nga gawas nga bahin hinay-hinay nga mangalukab! Gitawag kini nga exfoliation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worker weaver ants hold their larvae like little glue tubes, using the silk the larvae make
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: using the silk the larvae make to bind leaves together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not head, legs, or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: using the silk the larvae make to bind leaves together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en:
How do weaver ants glue leaves together?

Worker weaver ants hold their larvae like little glue tubes, using the silk the larvae make to bind leaves together!
copy.tl:
Paano idinidikit ng weaver ant ang mga dahon?

Hinahawakan ng manggagawang hantik ang kanilang mga larva at ginagamit ang sutlang gawa nito bilang pandikit ng mga dahon!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtapot sa weaver ant ang mga dahon?

Gigunitan sa mamumuong hantik ang ilang mga larva ug gigamit ang seda nga hinimo niini isip pandikit sa mga dahon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A weaverbird knows how to weave by instinct, but it gets better with practice
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes learned improvement in nest-building behavior, not an inherited change that better suits an environment (mimicry/camouflage). It shares the broad topic of animal behavior but does not support the competency's adaptation concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A weaverbird knows how to weave by instinct, but it gets better with practice
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal's instinct and practice, but does not describe growth, response, or reproduction—the specific characteristics listed in the competency. It is only tangentially related to living things.

copy.en:
Do weaverbirds learn to build nests?

A weaverbird knows how to weave by instinct, but it gets better with practice—older birds build neater nests!
copy.tl:
Natututo ba ang weaverbird gumawa ng pugad?

Likas nang alam ng weaverbird kung paano humabi, pero gumagaling pa rin ito sa pagsasanay—mas maayos ang pugad ng mas matandang ibon!
copy.bis:
Nakat-on ba ang weaverbird paghimo og salag?

Kinaiyanhon nga nahibalo ang weaverbird unsaon paghabi, apan mas maayo kini samtang nagpraktis—mas hapsay ang salag sa mas tigulang nga langgam!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You would weigh about one-sixth (1/6) of your Earth weight!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates that weight differs on the Moon due to weaker gravity, but the competency specifically targets gravity as a non-contact force affecting objects on Earth in predictable ways. The card does not identify gravity as a force nor address Earth-based behaviors, so it only shares the gravity topic without directly teaching this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: So 60 kg here feels like just 10 kg on the Moon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses kilograms as a unit, but it does not teach identifying or appropriately using units in simple science activities such as measuring with mg, g, kg, or degrees centigrade. The kilogram appears incidentally in a weight comparison, not as instruction on unit use.

copy.en:
How much would you weigh if you visited the Moon?

You would weigh about one-sixth (1/6) of your Earth weight! So 60 kg here feels like just 10 kg on the Moon.
copy.tl:
Magkano ang timbang mo kung bibisita ka sa Buwan?

Ang timbang mo ay halos isang-anim (1/6) ng timbang mo sa Daigdig! Kaya ang 60 kg dito ay parang 10 kg lang sa Buwan.
copy.bis:
Pila ang imong gibug-aton kung mobisita ka sa Bulan?

Ang imong gibug-aton mga ikaunom (1/6) lang sa imong gibug-aton sa Yuta! Busa ang 60 kg diri morag 10 kg ra sa Bulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The West Valley Fault is an active fault running right near Metro Manila!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use the PHIVOLCS FaultFinder or other reliable information source to identify where the nearest fault system is located from their community and assess the risk of earthquakes to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an active fault near Metro Manila but does not instruct using PHIVOLCS FaultFinder or another reliable source to identify the nearest fault system or assess risk. It only states a general fact, not the skill of locating/assessing via a source.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Families there must be ready for a possible strong earthquake.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: refer to the local disaster readiness plans to demonstrate what to do during and after an earthquake
assignedReviews.reason: The card says families must be ready but does not refer to local disaster readiness plans or demonstrate what to do during and after an earthquake. It only gives a general preparedness statement, not the specific competency action.

copy.en:
Why should families near Metro Manila prepare for earthquakes?

The West Valley Fault is an active fault running right near Metro Manila! Families there must be ready for a possible strong earthquake.
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat maghanda ang mga pamilya malapit sa Metro Manila sa lindol?

Ang West Valley Fault ay isang aktibong fault na dumadaan malapit sa Metro Manila! Kaya dapat maghanda ang mga pamilya doon sa posibleng malakas na lindol.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dapat mangandam ang mga pamilya duol sa Metro Manila para sa linog?

Ang West Valley Fault usa ka aktibo nga fault nga moagi duol sa Metro Manila! Busa dapat mangandam ang mga pamilya didto para sa posibleng kusog nga linog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A wetland sits right between dry land and open water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: The card only gives a general definition of a wetland. It does not describe biotic or abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, or coral reefs, and it does not use labeled diagrams as required.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A wetland sits right between dry land and open water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a wetland, which is a type of landform/water body, but it does not identify local examples or describe how such features influence living and non-living components of the environment.

copy.en: A wetland sits right between dry land and open water, acting like a perfect mix that shares features of both!
copy.tl: Ang wetland ay nasa pagitan ng tuyong lupa at bukas na tubig, kaya may halong katangian ng dalawa!
copy.bis: Ang wetland anaa sa tunga sa mala nga yuta ug bukas nga tubig, busa naay sagol nga kinaiya sa duha!
